Why the reminder outranks the flag. An overdue ITV has a date in the real world; a data disagreement has none. It waits. Why the queue is in the state machine at all rather than a permanent row: a permanent row would make Home grow a fifth thing that is usually empty, which is precisely how a calm surface becomes a dashboard. And the load-bearing consequence: All clear requires zero open flags, because this screen is Koi's promise and it must not be able to say "Everything OK" while two devices disagree in a drawer.

FIXTURE ARITHMETIC · TWO MORE CORRECTIONS
4 · ALSO COMING listed reminders outside its own 28-day bound

§2.2's own anatomy says the band "lists the rest of what falls inside the 28-day floor", then draws Oil & filter in 2 months and ITV in 8 months inside it. Those cannot both be right, and if the band can reach eight months out then All clear's "next few weeks" stops meaning anything. Taken: the stated rule. The band shows only what is inside 28 days, and when nothing else is, it does not render — which is what the Coming-up frame shows.

5 · The featured card named alerts that had already fired

Insurance defaults to 60/30/7-day alerts. On 28 July, with the renewal on 16 August, the 60- and 30-day alerts are in the past — so printing "Alerts 60, 30 and 7 days before" answers a question the user did not ask and implies three notifications are coming. §C1 asks for which alerts will fire, future tense. Corrected to "Next alert 9 August, 7 days before." The full rule lives on the reminder's own detail page, where the Anchor row makes it verifiable.

6 · The Last-fill card must lead with the car

§2.7's conditional fires whenever a second car exists — and the §0.6 fixture has two. So every frame here reads Golf GTI · 12 July · Repsol Tarragona, not the single-car form. Drawing the single-car version on a two-car fixture is the exact class of error that is correct in isolation and wrong here.

Both strings verbatim. No confetti, no streak, no "great job" — the app never performs enthusiasm. The one added row is All reminders ›: a state that says "quiet, not empty" must let you check.
Drawn in both themes because this is the brand moment, and because it is the frame where a bad dark palette shows first — the mark, the display voice and two ink steps all against the ground at once. Resolving the last flag while Home is on screen re-evaluates the state live, as a 150 ms fade: Home must not perform relief.

02 · The month pulse, and the one card that always follows

Three numbers, no chart, ever. Article 2 is constitutional and this strip is where it is easiest to break.
THE PULSE, AND ITS EMPTY STATE
JULY
412 km487,90 €1,18 €/km
A MONTH WITH NO READINGS IN IT YET
AUGUST
—0,00 €
No readings this month.
Money is genuinely 0,00 € — a real sum of zero records. Distance is not a sum Koi has grounds to state, so it never reads 0 km, and €/km disappears entirely rather than showing a dash. Three different treatments for three different truths, on one strip.
THE PULSE'S RULES
Scope
This calendar month, all live cars. Home carries no scope control at all — so this is fixed, never inherited from whichever chip another tab was left on.
The km rule
Newest reading inside the month, minus the last reading at or before its start. This is the one reading of the distance invariants that never invents distance for a period that has not finished — distinct from a completed Insights page, where the trail can bracket the whole window.
All three are ink
Mixed-kind money is a total, not a category — and distance was never money. No domain hue appears on this strip.
Never
A chart. A sparkline. A delta-vs-last-month arrow. A progress ring. Article 2.
Tapping it does nothing
It is a receipt, not a control. Considered and rejected: tapping into Insights' current-month page — it would make Home a dashboard entrance.
Arithmetic: 487,90 € ÷ 412 km = 1,1842 → 1,18 €/km. It reconciles with History's July whisper (3 fills · 487,90 €), with Insights' Cost headline, and with the Distance lens's 412 km · 14,7 km/day over 28 tracked days — 412 ÷ 28 = 14,71.
